page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-1 is an Arm-based virtual machine configured with 1 vCPU and 8.0 GB of system memory. Driven by a dedicated 3.4 GHz ARMv8 Neoverse-N3 processor core, the instance allocates 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and access to 112 MB of L3 cache. It operates with a high memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio of 8 GB per core, targeting lightweight workloads requiring elevated memory headroom rather than heavy multi-threaded compute. The instance includes hardware cryptographic acceleration through the AES instruction set, contains no local storage, and includes no GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a stark contrast between single-threaded efficiency and aggregate throughput. In single-threaded compression tests, the Neoverse-N3 architecture delivers strong results, achieving 32.47 GB/s in gzip compression. Single-core evaluations reflect competitive baseline performance, scoring 1711.0 in Geekbench and 2036.79 in stress-ng. However, because the instance features only a single hardware thread, multi-core metric rankings fall into the bottom 10 percentiles across PassMark, Geekbench, and stress-ng suites. Memory operations reflect moderate throughput, recording 23.47 GB/s read and 24.16 GB/s write speeds on large uncached blocks.

Given its single dedicated vCPU and lack of bundled local NVMe storage, n4a-highmem-1 represents a cost-efficient resource tier for specific small-scale deployments. It offers higher memory density per core than standard general-purpose tiers without requiring payment for excess compute threads. Workload suitability centers on low-volume in-memory caching, single-threaded backend services, staging databases, lightweight message brokering, and memory-bound utilities where multi-core scaling is unnecessary.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-1 is an entry-tier, memory-skewed virtual machine powered by a single 3.4 GHz ARMv8 Neoverse-N3 core and 8.0 GB of memory. Providing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, it offers a dedicated single-threaded compute profile backed by 2 MB of L2 cache and 112 MB of L3 cache. Hardware cryptographic acceleration is enabled via AES extensions. The configuration does not include GPUs or local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the architecture demonstrates competent single-core processing with strong single-threaded gzip compression at 32.47 GB/s and a Geekbench single-core score of 1711.0. Due to its single vCPU limitation, multi-core metrics sit in the lowest percentiles across standard test suites. The instance is suited for lightweight memory-centric workloads, including small in-memory caches, background utility workers, staging environments, and single-threaded network services requiring higher memory per core.
